builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DRVEXO-4B-Unified: Design and Evaluation of a Modular Speech-Vision System
summary: It replaces a pipeline of separate ASR, LLM, and TTS components with one 4B self-contained checkpoint using a temporal residual speech connector, boundary-delimited incremental synthesis, and task-conditioned scoring heads. The cost is adoption risk: weights and code are only planned for release, benchmarks are reported on validation sets without independent reproduction, and deployment needs a GPU capable of running a 4B multimodal model plus its audio encoders and decoders. It can fail on speech recognition robustness in noisy domains, on action-ranking accuracy for application-specific candidate sets, and on concurrency behavior outside the reported GB10 serving setup.
rationale: A single 4B multimodal checkpoint with tool-call and scoring interfaces fits a 24 GB GPU budget, but the reader must validate the promised open-weight release and reproduction quality before production commitment.

claims.statement: It replaces a pipeline of separate ASR, LLM, and TTS components with one 4B self-contained checkpoint using a temporal residual speech connector, boundary-delimited incremental synthesis, and task-conditioned scoring heads. The cost is adoption risk: weights and code are only planned for release, benchmarks are reported on validation sets without independent reproduction, and deployment needs a GPU capable of running a 4B multimodal model plus its audio encoders and decoders. It can fail on speech recognition robustness in noisy domains, on action-ranking accuracy for application-specific candidate sets, and on concurrency behavior outside the reported GB10 serving setup.

Reports 74.22% on MMMU validation (above published Gemma 3 4B IT and InternVL3.5-4B validation scores), 82.26% strict IFEval, and 89.40% on MATH-500, with 390 ms speech-synthesis first-chunk latency on one NVIDIA GB10.
